chunks: And the inmates of Paradise will call to the residents of Hell: 'We have found that the promise made to us by our Lord was true. Have you also found the promise of your Lord to be true?' They will answer: 'Yes (it is so).' Then a crier will call from among them: 'The curse of God be on the vile,'
ai.seo_question: What do the people of Paradise say to the people of Hell on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the finality of divine justice, where the inhabitants of Paradise invite the dwellers of Hell to witness the fulfillment of God's promise, leading to a divine proclamation of curse upon the unjust. The term 'Al-Zalimin' (the unjust) is interpreted broadly to include those who oppressed others and those who oppressed themselves through disbelief, emphasizing the comprehensive nature of divine retribution. This scene serves as a powerful reminder of the eternal separation between the righteous and the wicked, reinforcing the concept of 'Barzakh' as a precursor to the final judgment.
